sources.name: Premier League — Liverpool vs Nottingham Forest match statistics
sources.notes: Official league match-stat page. The accessible page shell did not expose its statistic values during this pass, so no candidate is attributed to it.

sources.name: Liverpool FC — Liverpool 2-2 Nottingham Forest: Analyse the game with Opta stats
sources.notes: Official club page identifies its embedded presentation as Opta data. The accessible text did not expose the embedded values, so it is retained for provenance without extracted candidates.

sources.name: Opta Analyst — Liverpool 2-2 Nottingham Forest stats
sources.notes: Opta match centre and post-match facts. The accessible article confirms that the embedded match centre contains Opta team and player data, but its tables were not available as extractable claims in this pass.

sources.name: Sky Sports — Liverpool vs Nottingham Forest match statistics
sources.notes: Explicit full-match team-stat tables expose possession, shots on target, accurate passes, accurate crosses, and related totals. The underlying measurement provider is not disclosed.

sources.name: TNT Sports — Liverpool vs Nottingham Forest statistics
sources.notes: Explicit full-match team-stat table exposes possession and shots on goal. It reports total passes and pass accuracy but not an explicit accurate-pass count; no accurate-pass value is inferred.

sources.name: StatMuse — Liverpool 2-2 Nottingham Forest
sources.notes: Structured match centre with lineup, formation, team statistics, and event data. The underlying measurement provider is not disclosed.

sources.name: Squawka — Liverpool vs Nottingham Forest post-match analysis
sources.notes: Post-match analysis with explicit player-level attacking facts and qualitative discussion of Liverpool's defensive issues; retained as supporting tactical context rather than a source for the posterior metrics.

sources.name: RFZ Football — Liverpool 2-2 Forest analysis
sources.notes: Qualitative phase-by-phase analysis describes Forest's 5-4-1 defensive block, Liverpool's slow first-half circulation, and second-half territorial pressure. Time-specific possession claims are not treated as full-match candidates.

shots_on_target_per_match.evidence_location: Match Stats > Key Stats > Shots on target

shots_on_target_per_match.notes: Conflicts with Sky Sports and StatMuse despite the same apparent full-match team scope.

accurate_crosses_per_match.rationale: Independent measurement providers report the same compatible value.

accurate_passes_per_match.rationale: No strict majority exists; this is the arithmetic mean of compatible independent provider values and must be labeled as derived when reviewed.

formation.rationale: At least two independent measurement providers are required.

possession_pct.rationale: No strict majority exists; this is the arithmetic mean of compatible independent provider values and must be labeled as derived when reviewed.

shots_on_target_per_match.rationale: A strict majority of independent measurement providers report this value.

notes: This is a delayed research draft and cannot update the production observation or posterior without human review and promotion.
Sky Sports, TNT Sports, and StatMuse disagree on Liverpool's full-match possession: 69.1%, 70%, and 69%, respectively.

TNT Sports reports six shots on goal, while Sky Sports and StatMuse each report four shots on target; the resolver may select the strict majority, but the terminology conflict remains flagged for human review.
Sky Sports reports 562 accurate passes and StatMuse reports 566; TNT Sports exposes only total passes and rounded pass accuracy, so no completed-pass value is inferred from that source.
Sky Sports and StatMuse agree on five accurate crosses.
Only StatMuse exposes an explicit nominal starting formation in accessible text, so formation lacks independent corroboration.
No explicit compatible PPDA value was found. Qualitative descriptions of pressing, tempo, or territorial control are not converted into PPDA.
Underlying provider independence is not disclosed by the structured match centres and must be checked during human review.
